pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A gourd rattle makes sound because (1 mark)
   A. the seeds inside knock against the walls
   B. air is blown through it
   C. strings are plucked
   D. a bow is rubbed

2. Claves are (1 mark)
   A. a kind of flute
   B. a horn
   C. two wooden sticks hit together
   D. drums with strings

3. What does the word indigenous mean? (1 mark)
   A. Made in a factory
   B. Very new
   C. Belonging to a people and place from long ago
   D. Brought from another continent

4. To improvise a rhythmic pattern means to (1 mark)
   A. make it up on the spot
   B. stay silent
   C. write it before playing
   D. copy it from a book only

5. Macramé is a technique of (1 mark)
   A. beating drums
   B. tying knots to make patterns and shapes
   C. painting on cloth
   D. carving wood

6. Which is a rule break in netball? (1 mark)
   A. Pivoting on one foot
   B. Pushing another player
   C. Passing to a teammate
   D. Catching with two hands

7. A full netball court is divided into how many equal parts? (1 mark)
   A. Two
   B. Four
   C. Three
   D. Six

8. In netball, the ball is moved mainly by (1 mark)
   A. running with it
   B. passing it
   C. rolling it
   D. kicking it

9. To paint an object so it looks round, you should (1 mark)
   A. paint a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side
   B. use one flat colour only
   C. paint it black
   D. leave it blank

10. What do you add to a colour to make it darker? (1 mark)
   A. Black
   B. Yellow
   C. White
   D. Water only

11. A montage is (1 mark)
   A. a painting with only one colour
   B. a song
   C. a drawing in charcoal
   D. a picture made by joining many cut pieces on a background

12. Which is the first step in mixing green? (1 mark)
   A. Use only water
   B. Use only white
   C. Put red and black on the palette
   D. Put yellow and blue on the palette

13. A rhythmic pattern feels finished when it ends on (1 mark)
   A. a mistake
   B. a very short note
   C. a long note
   D. a rest

14. Which of these letters has a tail below the baseline? (1 mark)
   A. l
   B. y
   C. h
   D. d

15. What joins the stems of a pair of quavers? (1 mark)
   A. A rest
   B. A rope
   C. A beam
   D. A bar of soap

16. Repeating a small group of notes in a rhythm helps listeners to (1 mark)
   A. stop listening
   B. remember the pattern
   C. change the words
   D. forget the pattern

17. Why do we knead clay before using it? (1 mark)
   A. To make it smooth and remove air
   B. To make it hard
   C. To make it dry
   D. To make it black

18. Which move skips over a note? (1 mark)
   A. r to m
   B. d to r
   C. m to r
   D. d to m

19. How do you make a coil? (1 mark)
   A. Beat it with a stick
   B. Roll a small piece between the palms or on a table
   C. Cut it flat
   D. Bake it

20. The middle note of d, r and m is (1 mark)
   A. d
   B. none
   C. m
   D. r

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how to make flour paste glue. (3 marks)

22. Describe how to make a chest pass. (4 marks)

23. Explain how to write a rhythm from dictation. (3 marks)

24. What are ascenders and descenders in lettering? Give one example of each. (3 marks)

25. Describe how to play a mini-netball game safely and fairly from warm-up to the end. (5 marks)

26. Explain what tone or value means in a drawing. (3 marks)

27. Explain how to tie an overhand knot. (3 marks)

28. Describe how to make a value scale strip of orange. (3 marks)

29. Give three safety measures to observe when playing netball. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — the seeds inside knock against the walls
   When shaken, seeds inside hit the gourd and make a sound.

2. C — two wooden sticks hit together
   Claves are two hardwood sticks that are struck together.

3. C — Belonging to a people and place from long ago
   Indigenous instruments belong to a community and were made from local materials.

4. A — make it up on the spot
   Improvising is inventing a pattern without preparing it first.

5. B — tying knots to make patterns and shapes
   Macramé is done by tying cords in knots.

6. B — Pushing another player
   Contact such as pushing is not allowed.

7. C — Three
   A netball court is divided into three equal thirds.

8. B — passing it
   Players may not run with the ball, so they pass it to move it forward.

9. A — paint a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side
   Tones make an object look solid and round.

10. A — Black
   Black makes a shade, a darker tone.

11. D — a picture made by joining many cut pieces on a background
   A montage joins many pictures or pieces to make one whole picture.

12. D — Put yellow and blue on the palette
   Green comes from yellow and blue.

13. C — a long note
   Ending on a crotchet, a long note, makes it sound complete.

14. B — y
   The letter y has a tail below the baseline.

15. C — A beam
   A thick line called a beam joins them.

16. B — remember the pattern
   Repetition gives shape and makes the rhythm easier to remember.

17. A — To make it smooth and remove air
   Kneading makes clay smooth and easy to shape.

18. D — d to m
   Going from d to m skips r.

19. B — Roll a small piece between the palms or on a table
   Rolling back and forth makes a long even coil.

20. D — r
   Ray lies between doh and me.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Mix flour with a little cold water to a smooth paste. An adult adds hot water while stirring. Let it cool before use.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold the ball at chest height with both hands. Look at the partner. Step forward and straighten the arms, turning the thumbs down. The ball goes to the partner's chest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen twice to the pattern. Count the beats. For each beat decide if it was one long sound, two short sounds or silence, and write taa, ta-te or a rest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: An ascender is the part of a letter that goes up above the small letters, such as b. A descender goes below the baseline, such as p.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning, 1 mark for correct examples.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: Warm up with jogging and stretching. Choose fair teams and positions. Check the ground and the ball. Move into space, pass early and play your position. Follow the rules, obey the umpire and thank the other team.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each stage: warm-up, fair teams, checking, playing skills, fair ending.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tone means how light or dark an area is. In a charcoal drawing, we can make tones from light grey to black by pressing lightly or hard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for lightness or darkness, 1 mark for range of tones, 1 mark for charcoal pressure.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Make a loop with the cord. Pass the end through the loop. Pull both ends to tighten.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Draw a strip and divide it into five boxes. Mix orange with white for the two light boxes. Paint pure orange in the middle. Mix orange with black for the two dark boxes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the five boxes, 1 mark for light tones, 1 mark for dark tones.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Remove jewellery, cut long nails, warm up, wear proper shoes, play on flat ground. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each measure.
